about: An arrow whose head is sized to its line: straight or curved (bend), or routed at right angles for flowcharts and architecture (route elbow or corner, with rounded turns); dashed, open or filled head, double-ended, an optional label beside the middle, and flow (animated dashes moving along it) for movement of blood, water, data or energy. As a link it runs between the anchors; in a module between data.from and data.to.

bend.description: curvature as a fraction of length, positive bending left of the direction of travel; for elbow, how far along the cross segment moves (-0.5 to 0.5)

route.description: curve follows bend; elbow runs at right angles, leaving and arriving along the sides of the modules its anchors sit on; corner turns exactly once

first.description: for elbow and corner, the axis it leaves along; auto follows the side its anchor sits on, else the longer axis

radius.description: rounding of elbow and corner turns

label.description: a few words beside the middle

labelSide.description: which side of the line the label sits

width.description: line width; defaults to the stroke token

about: A short label in the work's font with a paper-coloured halo that keeps it legible over pictures and lines; multi-line with \n and an optional smaller note underneath. For naming things on the canvas without boxes.

Names a part the textbook way: a thin leader line from a small dot on the part to the label. The module spans from the part to the text; target is the named point in the module (0..1) and side says where the text sits.

target.description: the named point {x,y} 0..1; defaults to the edge opposite the text

about: A soft elliptical contact shadow that sets a picture on the ground instead of letting it float. A flat module just under the object's base, about as wide as the object.
Places a picture material fitted by its visible content, optionally grounded with a soft shadow and captioned underneath. The quickest way to put a found or generated picture on the canvas.

fit.description: contain shows the whole picture; cover fills the box

about: A small numbered circle that gives reading order or marks the steps along a path.

Curved arrows running round a circle: the shape of any cycle (water, life, seasons, feedback). Step i sits at angle start + i·360/n on the circle, so stage pictures can be placed there as their own modules; labels optional.

steps.description: labels of the stages, or a count

start.description: angle of the first stage in degrees (-90 is the top)

gap.description: degrees left free around each stage

about: Axes with nicely rounded ticks and one or more curves: functions of x given as JavaScript expressions ("Math.sin(x)", "2*Math.PI*Math.sqrt(x/9.8)") or measured points. An optional marker shows the current value; set it from a slider to make the plot interactive. For laws, quantities and comparisons over a range.

x.description: {min, max, label, ticks (count or list), format ('{} m')}

series.description: [{fn: 'expression in x'} or {points: [[x,y]]}, label, color, width, dashed, dots}]

marker.description: the current value on the first curve {x, label?, color?}: a dot with guides to both axes; update it with api.set

about: A time axis with events: dots on the line, dates beside it, names alternating above and below so neighbours never collide; an event can carry a note and be accented.

events.description: [{at: number, date?: shown text, label, note?, accent?}]

from.description: start of the axis; defaults to the first event

to.description: end of the axis; defaults to the last event

about: A curly brace that gathers the things beside it, its point toward facing (right, left, up, down), with a label at the point. For grouping without a box.
A soft organic area that marks a zone (a habitat, a layer, a sphere of influence) without drawing a box: a seeded irregular translucent blob filling the module, optional label and texture effect.

effect.description: an effect id for texture, e.g. watercolor-edge

about: Rows of gentle waves for water, a river, or a sound or light wave; they roll slowly unless still is set.
An orbit: a fine ellipse filling the module, with an optional body (a picture material id) travelling along it, counter-clockwise like planets seen from above the north pole unless clockwise is set.

body.description: picture material id travelling on the orbit

period.description: seconds per revolution; 0 keeps it still

phase.description: starting position 0..1 (0 is the right end)

about: A labelled slider for one quantity, showing its value and unit. It keeps its own position while dragged and sends "change" with the number: listen with api.on(moduleId, "change", v => …) in the scene interaction and update other modules with api.set.

A row of options of which one is chosen: seasons, stages, modes or steps of a story. It marks its own choice and sends "change" with {option, index}: listen with api.on(moduleId, "change", c => …) and show the chosen state with api.set or api.move.

A block of a flowchart, architecture or concept map: a box, pill, circle, decision diamond, database cylinder or document holding a title, an optional note and an optional icon, coloured by the style. One per module, joined by arrow links (route elbow for flowcharts) so blocks move on their own and connections follow; the words wrap inside the shape.

shape.description: box for a step or component, pill for start/end, diamond for a decision, cylinder for a store

fillStyle.description: soft tint, solid colour or paper; plain defaults to none, other tones to soft

icon.description: an icon or small picture beside or above the words

dashed.description: a dashed outline, for something optional or external

lift.description: a soft shadow that lifts the block off the paper

effect.description: an effect id applied to the shape, such as rough-edge

about: A hierarchy as a tidy tree: an organisation, taxonomy, or a goal or system broken into parts. The root is filled, its children tinted, deeper levels outlined, joined by rounded right-angle lines; any node can carry a note or be accented. Grows down or right and spreads to fill the module.

color.description: the root's colour; defaults to accent

lineColor.description: the connecting lines; defaults to muted

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: Stacked layers from top to bottom: a software architecture, protocol stack or the tiers of an organisation. Each band names its layer on the left with an optional note and lays its parts out as chips across the rest; a band without parts centres its name; a layer can be accented.

layers.description: top first: [{label, note?, items?: [names of its parts], accent?}]

color.description: the bands' tint; defaults to accent2

labelWidth.description: width of the name column; 0 or unset fits the names

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A two-by-two matrix: two axes from low to high split the plane into four named quadrants (urgent and important, cost and value, risk and impact), items as labelled dots at their positions, one quadrant optionally highlighted.

quadrants.description: names in reading order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right

items.description: [{x: 0..1, y: 0..1, label, accent?}] placed from low to high

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A comparison table: options as columns, criteria as rows; true and false show as a tick and a dash, other values as words; one column can be highlighted as the recommended or subject option. Rules between rows only, no grid, so it reads as a figure.

columns.description: the options compared, as column headings

rows.description: [{label, values: [one per column: text, number, true or false]}]

highlight.description: index of the highlighted column, -1 for none

corner.description: an optional heading above the criteria

about: Levels stacked as a pyramid (a hierarchy of needs, a food chain, a share that narrows upwards) or a funnel (stages that narrow downwards, such as conversion). Bands shade from accent to accent2, solid or soft; notes stand to the right on dotted leaders.

shape.description: narrow at the top, or narrowing downwards

fillStyle.description: solid bands with paper words, or tinted ones

color.description: the top band; defaults to accent

color2.description: the bottom band; defaults to accent2

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: Two or three overlapping sets: each circle tinted in its own colour so the overlaps deepen, each name in the part that belongs to that set alone, with an optional note, and an optional name for the shared middle.

sets.description: two or three: [{label, note?, color?}] or names

overlap.description: the name of the shared middle

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A mind map: a central idea with branches to either side, each branch in its own colour, its points written on the ends of curved lines. For brainstorms, the facets of a topic and outlines.

branches.description: [{label, children?: [points], color?}]; the first half go right, the rest left

color.description: the centre's fill; defaults to ink

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A process as numbered steps on a track: circles joined by a line, each name beside its number with an optional note. Given current, earlier steps show done, the current one ringed and later ones in outline. Runs across or down.

current.description: index of the step in progress; -1 shows all alike

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: Swimlanes: parallel bands, one per actor, team or system, each named in its header, as the background of a cross-functional process; place the steps over it as node modules joined by arrow links. Lanes run across (rows) or down (columns); one can be accented.

lanes.description: [{label, note?, accent?}] or names, first at the top or left

direction.description: lanes as rows or as columns

header.description: width or height of the header; unset fits the names

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A bar chart for comparing a few quantities: rounded bars on a baseline, the value at each bar's end and the name at its foot, no grid; an accented bar stands out while the rest share one colour. Upright or lying (for long names and rankings).

max.description: the value of a full bar; defaults to the largest

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: Parts of a whole as a donut, or a pie with hole 0: each slice in its own style colour, named outside on a short leader with its share (or a note), and a headline or total in the middle. For budgets, compositions and survey answers.

items.description: [{label, value, note?: shown instead of the percentage, color?}]

hole.description: size of the hole; 0 for a pie

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A gauge: a half-ring scale from min to max with the value filled in and a needle, the number and unit in the middle, optional coloured zones and a label. For a reading on a scale: speed, temperature, a score or a percentage.

value.description: the reading; set it from a slider to animate

zones.description: [{from, to, color?}] bands on the scale

color.description: the filled part; defaults to accent

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A key figure: one large number with its unit and what it counts, an optional change marked with an up or down triangle (coloured by whether that is good), and a note. For headline numbers beside a figure or a row of them as a summary.

trend.description: direction of the change; defaults to its sign

good.description: which direction is good, coloured accent2; the other is accent

about: A fishbone (cause and effect) diagram: the effect in a head at the right, a spine running to it, and slanted bones above and below for the categories of cause, each with its causes written on short ribs. For root-cause analysis.

problem.description: the problem or result, in the head

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A sequence diagram: participants across the top with dashed lifelines, messages as arrows between them in time order, replies dashed with open heads, a message to oneself as a loop; optionally numbered. Drawn in the style, unlike a generic renderer.

actors.description: participant names, left to right, or [{label, accent?}]

messages.description: [{from, to: participant names, label, reply?, accent?}] in time order

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A schedule as a Gantt chart: tasks in rows with names on the left and rounded bars from start to end on a shared time axis; a task can be accented, done ones fade, a milestone (no end) is a diamond, and a dashed line can mark now.

tasks.description: [{label, start, end?: none for a milestone, accent?, done?}]

from.description: start of the axis; defaults to the earliest start

to.description: end of the axis; defaults to the latest end

ticks.description: [{at, label}] marks on the axis; defaults to whole numbers

now.description: where to draw the now line

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A speech or annotation bubble: words wrapping inside a rounded bubble whose tail points at what they are about, from any side at any point along it, with an optional speaker. For a person's line, a thought or a remark beside a picture.

tail.description: the side the tail leaves from

fillStyle.description: paper inside, or filled with the colour

dashed.description: a dashed outline, for a thought

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A checklist: items in rows with ticked or open boxes, or numbers or bullets; done items softened and struck through, each with an optional note. For requirements, to-dos, criteria and key points.

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A radar chart: several qualities on spokes from a centre, a web of rings for the scale, and each subject as a translucent shape joining its scores, with a legend when there are several, so profiles compare at a glance.

axes.description: names of the qualities, clockwise from the top

max.description: the score at the outer ring

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: Concentric rings, innermost first: a core and the layers around it (golden circle, an onion model, self to society). The core is accent and the rings accent2 growing paler outwards, each name in its own band, the core's in its middle; bottom-aligned they nest like bubbles.

rings.description: [{label, note?, color?}] or names, innermost first

align.description: share a centre, or stand on one bottom

color2.description: the outer ring; defaults to accent2

effect.description: an effect id for the shapes' texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain

about: A true map from real geographic data, from the whole world down to a few streets: coastlines, lakes and named rivers, and in a city view (a few dozen kilometres or less) OpenStreetMap's streets, waterways, parks and railways with the names of main roads, so a walk or tour through one town lands on its real streets; optionally today's country borders (disputed lines drawn as such) and first-level divisions such as provinces and states. Places, routes and areas are given in longitude and latitude, so everything lands where it really is, across the 180th meridian too; labels keep clear of each other and of the routes. Routes take place names or [lon, lat] points, with width, colour, dashes and direction arrows; areas shade a territory; highlights pick out named rivers, whole or between two places. Change it through these parameters rather than reaching into what it draws, whose structure is not fixed. The view fits bounds [west, south, east, north] or everything placed, and the colours follow the style.

places.description: [{name, lon, lat, note?, kind?: town|capital|battle|mountain|pass|water|region, major?, label?: right|left|above|below|top-right|…, color?, picture?, pictureSize?}]; water and region are names without a marker

routes.description: [{points: place names or [lon, lat], label?, note?, color?, width?, style?: solid|dashed|dotted, arrow?: end|along|none, labelSide?}]; draw one route per stage or force to vary colour and width

areas.description: [{points: [lon, lat] or place names, color?, opacity?}], a shaded territory; name it with a region place

highlights.description: [{river: a name or names as the map labels them (a main stream's reaches can have their own names), color?, width?, from?, to?: place names or [lon, lat]}]; picks out real rivers, whole or the stretch between from and to, as far as the data names them (a wide estuary may be unnamed)

bounds.description: [west, south, east, north] in degrees; defaults to everything placed with room around it

borders.description: today's borders: countries, or countries with their first-level divisions (provinces, states). Leave none for a historical map unless modern borders help locate it, and say so

borderColor.description: colour of the border lines; defaults to a grey from the style

rivers.description: rivers with or without their names

streets.description: in a city view, OpenStreetMap's streets, waterways, parks and railways as the ground; false keeps the plain coast and rivers

roadNames.description: in a city view, the names of main roads where they fit

language.description: language of the river, country and division names

edge.description: a thin frame, or edges that fade into the paper

water.description: sea and lake colour; defaults to a pale tint of the style's cool colour

land.description: land colour; defaults to a faint tint of paper

effect.description: an effect id for the land's texture, such as the style's rough-edge or pencil-grain
